args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) per FIN-212

The implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP while the test suite and FIN-212
expect banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN). This caused the nightly
build to fail on tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to implement banker's rounding per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using ROUND_HALF_UP.

## Changes
- Replaced `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `src/money.py`, so `round_money` now rounds half-values to the nearest even cent, e.g. `2.675 -> 2.68` (nearest even digit 8 is already even)

args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using ROUND_HALF_UP, so e.g. `Decimal("2.665")` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `round_money`, matching the documented FIN-212 requirement and the behavior asserted in `tests/test_money.py`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` (commit 08d3cd5986): **passed**.
